summary: Configured and verified a persistent firewalld policy on node1. SSH is allowed globally; TCP 9000 is allowed only from node2 (10.100.130.11/32) and rejected from node3 and all other IPv4/IPv6 sources. All three nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Added ordered permanent firewalld rich rules for TCP 9000.
Verified node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was rejected; SSH remained reachable from both.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time and verified changed boot IDs and service recovery.
Confirmed runtime and permanent rules survived node1's restart.
Removed the temporary port-9000 verification listener.

evidence.summary: Runtime and permanent rules allow node2/32 first, reject every other IPv4 source, reject IPv6, and retain the global SSH service.
Node2 reached TCP 9000 with HTTP 200; node3 was refused; both reached SSH and received an OpenSSH banner.
Shows healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered firewalld/SSH/rules, and restored allow/reject behavior.
Shows healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, active SSH, and recovered authorized access to node1:9000.
Shows healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, active SSH, and continued rejection from node1:9000.
